blocks.text: Map.get()
You get the value of a key in a map with the get() method
fruits.get("apples");
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Map.set()
You can add elements to a map with the set() method:

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The set() method can also be used to change existing map values:
fruits.set("apples", 500);
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Map.size
The size property returns the number of elements in a map:
fruits.size;
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Map.delete()
The delete() method removes a map element:
fruits.delete("apples");
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Map.clear()
The clear() method removes all the elements from a map:
fruits.clear();
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Map.has()
The has() method returns true if a key exists in a map:
fruits.has("apples");
blocks.caption: Example

Being able to use objects as keys is an important Map feature.

blocks.text: Remember: The key is an object (apples), not a string ("apples"):

blocks.text: JavaScript Map.groupBy()
ES2024 added the Map.groupBy() method to JavaScript.

The Map.groupBy() method groups the elements of an iterable according
to the values returned from a callback function.
The Map.groupBy() method does not change the original object.
The return value is a Map with a key for each group, where each key is assigned to an Array of the associated elements.

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Browser Support
Map.groupBy() is an ECMAScript 2024 feature.

JavaScript 2024 is supported in new browsers since
March 2024:
Warning
ES2024 features are relatively new.
Older browsers may need an alternative code (Polyfill)
Object.groupBy() vs Map.groupBy()
The difference between Object.groupBy() and Map.groupBy() is:
Object.groupBy() groups elements into a JavaScript object.
Map.groupBy() groups elements into a Map object.
